intended_object: An auxiliary device: the n-fold iterate of the functor F ↦ coker(F → C⁰(F)), where C⁰(F) is the flasque envelope (the sheaf of discontinuous sections). Its only role is to build the functorial (Godement-style) flasque resolution in degree n. Inferred from the docstring and from how flasqueResolutionFunctor and flasqueResolutionDifferential use it.
explanation:
The definition is an intermediate step in building the Godement resolution of a sheaf of abelian groups. Iterate 0 is the identity functor. Iterate n+1 is iterate n followed by taking the cokernel of the flasque-envelope map. Writing Zⁿ for the n-th iterate, the degree-n term of the resolution is C⁰(Zⁿ(F)). The differential is the composite C⁰(Zⁿ) → Zⁿ⁺¹ → C⁰(Zⁿ⁺¹).

The recursion matches this standard construction exactly. Composing on the right with flasqueEnvelopeQuotientFunctor, which applies the quotient after iterate n, is the correct order.

Still, the iterated cokernel functor is internal scaffolding for the resolution. It is not a standard named mathematical object to be judged on its own terms, so it falls under `not_a_mathematical_object`. Read instead as "the iterated cokernel functor", it would be faithful. Its restriction to TopCat.{0} and AddCommGrpCat is fixed by the surrounding file, not by this definition.
